name: Pohnpei White-eye
rangeDescription: Pohnpei (eastern caroline islands)
description: Small gray bird endemic to Pohnpei, in the Caroline Islands of Micronesia. Uniform plumage makes it unmistakable on the island; Caroline Islands White-eye is yellowish overall, while Long-billed White-eye is greenish with a much longer bill.

name: Malabar Pied-Hornbill
rangeDescription: Mixed forest of southern india and sri lanka
description: A large black-and-white hornbill with a huge bill and casque. The plumage is almost entirely black, but for the white on the belly and the sides of the throat.

name: Bearded Wood-Partridge
rangeDescription: Humid montane forest of northeastern mexico
description: Very elusive, chickenlike bird of humid evergreen forest in foothills and highlands; scarce and very local in eastern Mexico where it is endemic. Usually in pairs or small groups on the forest floor.

name: Javan Banded-Pitta
rangeDescription: Java and bali
description: Beautiful ground-dweller with black mask, clean white throat, and finely barred underparts. Male has an egg-yolk-yellow eyebrow, royal-blue “bib”, and black crown.

name: Cordoba Cinclodes
rangeDescription: Andes of north-central argentina (western córdoba to eastern tucumán)
description: Small-billed cinclodes of the Sierra de Comenchingones in central Argentina. Disperses to adjacent lowlands during the nonbreeding season.

name: Baer's Pochard
rangeDescription: Breeds northeastern asia; winters to southern china and southeastern asia
description: Extremely rare diving duck. Breeding male has a dark green gloss to the head, but often seems dark-headed in poor lighting.

name: Black-capped Sparrow
rangeDescription: Dry deciduous forest and scrub of lowlands and hills on pacific slope from manabí in west-central ecuador southward to cajamarca in northwestern peru
description: Beautiful sparrow with gray upperparts, and black mask and crown separated by a white stripe. Similar to male Collared Warbling-Finch, but breast band is smaller, face stripe does not reach past the front of the eye, and tail lacks white.

name: Spix's Macaw
rangeDescription: Palm groves of northeastern brazil (northern bahia); on verge of extinction
description: Now declared extinct in the wild; only a few individuals survive in captivity. Medium-sized macaw with grayish head shading to deep glaucous blue in the rest of the plumage, contrasting with the black sturdy bill.

name: Cocos Finch
rangeDescription: Forest of cocos island (off western costa rica)
description: Plump, short-tailed bird found only on Cocos Island, located in the Pacific Ocean about 300 miles southwest of mainland Costa Rica. Sexes look quite different.

name: Basra Reed Warbler
rangeDescription: Southern iraq (tigris and euphrates valleys); winters kenya to malawi
description: Medium-sized Acrocephalus warbler with cold gray-olive-brown plumage and whitish underparts. Note the long and slender bill and the short eyebrow that reaches just behind the eye.

name: Santa Marta Antpitta
rangeDescription: Santa marta mountains (northeastern colombia)
description: Plump, terrestrial bird found only in the Santa Marta Mountains of Colombia. Like other antpittas, it is short-tailed and long-legged.

name: Thick-billed Berrypecker
rangeDescription: New guinea (mountains of bird's head peninsula and central highlands)
description: A small, rare bird of mid-montane forest. Male is dark gray above and pale gray below with a slight, pale tuft on the side.

name: Jamaican Pewee
rangeDescription: Jamaica
description: A small, plain woodland species often found flycatching from exposed perches at middle levels in the forest; often flicks tail once upon landing. Note that this species has relatively inconspicuous wingbars and no eyering.

name: Plum-throated Cotinga
rangeDescription: Lowlands of southeastern colombia to northern bolivia and western amazonian brazil
description: Bright blue cotinga of lowland rainforest. Males are pure sky blue, with a purple throat and light eye; females are buffy tan with faint scalloping.

name: Banded Cotinga
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (southern bahia and minas gerais to rio de janeiro)
description: Jaw-droppingly beautiful bird. Males are cobalt-blue and purple, while females are dusky brown above with white scaling and buff below with dark spots.

name: Snowy Sheathbill
rangeDescription: Southern argentina, southern chile, antarctic peninsula, and falkland islands
description: Unique, stocky, and rather pigeonlike white bird (actually an aberrant shorebird) of Antarctic Peninsula and islands. Migrates north in winter to Tierra del Fuego and southern Argentina, where a few immatures remain year-round at sea lion and penguin colonies.

name: Flat-billed Vireo
rangeDescription: Semiarid lowland scrub of hispaniola including gonâve island
description: A small, slow-moving species that prefers dry brush and scrublands where it typically feeds low and sometimes even on the ground; sometimes found at higher elevations where it can be found feeding in or near the canopy in vine tangles. The Flat-billed Vireo is a relatively plain species, with bold white wingbars, and whitish eyes.

name: Pirre Chlorospingus
rangeDescription: Humid montane forest of eastern panama
description: Fairly small tanager-like sparrow with an extremely tiny range in the foothills of eastern Panama, from around 800–1,200 m. Distinctive in range: olive-brownish overall with brighter yellow-ochre underparts, darker blackish face, and staring pale eye.

name: Medium Egret
rangeDescription: Japan to southern india and greater sundas
description: A stocky egret that is larger than Eastern Cattle and Little Egrets, but smaller than the Great Egret. Often confusing and difficult to identify, this bird is truly intermediate between potential confusion species.

name: Peruvian Piedtail
rangeDescription: Subtropical southeastern peru (huánuco, pasco, puno, and cusco)
description: Small hummingbird found in montane forest, especially on outlying ridges of the Andes. Green above with orange sides and a white belly that extends onto the sides of its neck; it gets its name from its bold black-and-white striped tail pattern, which is especially visible in flight.
